tickets.title: Add cpal as an optional dependency behind the cpal-input feature and implement device-backed capture returning Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError> with an integration test

contracts.precondition: cpal is an optional dependency reachable only through the `cpal-input` feature (default build graph contains no cpal). The RFC §40 signature exists behind #[cfg(feature = "cpal-input")]: `pub async fn open_default_microphone_source(format: AudioFormat) -> Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError>`. The input `format` is a validated AudioFormat (AudioFormat::new succeeded; sample_rate ∈ {Hz8000, Hz16000, Hz24000, Hz48000}, bit_depth ∈ {I16, F32}, channel_layout ∈ {Mono, StereoInOut}, frame_ms ∈ {10, 20, 40, 60}).
contracts.postcondition: When a default input device exists and its native sample format is convertible to the i16 pipeline contract, open_default_microphone_source returns Ok(Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>) whose next_chunk fills the caller's &mut [i16] buffer with captured PCM and returns the written sample count. Device-open, format-mismatch, build-stream, and play failures surface as Err(SipError) (SipErrorKind::NativeError for device/stream errors; SipErrorKind::AudioFormatUnsupported for non-convertible sample formats) — never a panic.
contracts.invariant: The returned source is AsyncAudioSource + Send and can be stored as Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send> in AudioMixer (ErasedAudioSource auto-derived via blanket impl). Sample conversion clamps into the valid i16 range (no wraparound). With `cpal-input` disabled, the function, the CpalMicrophoneSource type, and the cpal crate are compiled out of the build.

contracts.precondition: Audio subscribe uses sources — AudioMixer stores Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>; AsyncAudioSource trait is defined as #[async_trait::async_trait] pub trait AsyncAudioSource: Send { async fn next_chunk(&mut self, buf: &mut [i16]) -> usize; }.
contracts.postcondition: ErasedAudioSource blanket impl auto-derived for all T: AsyncAudioSource + Send; SyncAudioSource trait and SyncSourceAdapter<T: SyncAudioSource + Send> provided for synchronous sources; any new concrete source (e.g. CpalMicrophoneSource) implementing AsyncAudioSource + Send automatically gains ErasedAudioSource.
contracts.invariant: ErasedAudioSource auto-derived for every AsyncAudioSource implementor — blanket impl <T: AsyncAudioSource + Send> ErasedAudioSource for T must compile. SyncSourceAdapter<T: SyncAudioSource + Send> must implement AsyncAudioSource + Send. CpalMicrophoneSource must implement AsyncAudioSource + Send so it is usable as Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>.

[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

One or more ABC violations were confirmed (O-001, major). This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation. Every violation must be fully resolved, and every contract must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

### Goal
Resolve O-001 and finalize the real cpal device-backed microphone source: keep `open_default_microphone_source` (src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:173-179) returning `Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError>` backed by the platform default microphone behind the `cpal-input` feature, and close the ABC gap by unit-testing every error path (map_default_config_error / map_supported_configs_error / map_build_stream_error / map_play_error) and the unsupported-sample-format arm of build_input_stream, with the feature-gated integration test retained.

### Purpose
The `cpal-input` feature has been wired since P8-7 (Cargo.toml: `cpal-input = ["dep:cpal"]`), and the microphone source is the only RFC-required audio source that is device-backed. Downstream consumers (AudioMixer via P5-2, the audio_tap example via P8-6, AI TTS source insertion) rely on opening the default microphone as an AsyncAudioSource. The ABC inspection confirmed the happy-path machinery is complete but the error-contract (never-panic / typed-Err) is not enforced by any test — O-001 must be closed so the contract is provable.

### Motivation
P8-4 delivered the AsyncAudioSource adapter machinery under a no-new-dependencies constraint; P8-7 landed the cpal dependency and real capture, resolving the `[::STUB::] P8-7` marker. What remains is the ABC-mandated O-001 closure: cpal 0.18.1 exposes publicly constructible `cpal::Error` and `SupportedStreamConfig`, so the error paths are unit-testable without a device — the omission is a test-coverage defect, not an architectural limit. This ticket removes that defect and re-proves C051/C033.

### Constraints
- cpal must be an optional dependency reachable only via `cpal-input`; default builds must not pull the cpal crate (feature-additive invariant). Cargo.toml:40 already declares `check-cfg = ['cfg(feature, values("cpal-input"))']`.
- MSRV is 1.95; pin a cpal version whose API is stable and documented — cpal 0.18.1 (Cargo.lock) requires an explicit `stream.play()` after build and pins the sample rate/config explicitly.
- The public `open_default_microphone_source` signature must not change (C051 precondition); the returned source must implement AsyncAudioSource + Send.
- No panics on device failure — all errors map to SipError (NativeError for device/stream, AudioFormatUnsupported for non-convertible sample formats). The O-001 unit tests must make a regression detectable.
- CI without audio hardware must not run the device integration test by default (#[ignore] + SI_PRS_TEST_AUDIO=1 gate).

This is not a case of 'deterministic yet fundamentally untestable' (an architectural defect): the deterministic core is fully extracted and unit-tested. Alternative verification: unit tests on the pure helpers; #[ignore] device test.

Reason: the device layer is a thin boundary and all deterministic logic (select_input_config preference, sample-format match, error mapping, queue handoff) is covered by synthetic SampleQueue / pure-helper unit tests. This is not an architectural defect: the nondeterminism lives only at the device boundary, not in the crate's own logic. Alternative verification: error-mapping functions are unit-tested; the device integration test is #[ignore] where no default device exists.

Reason: the device-open logic is thin and every non-environmental decision (sample-format match, error mapping, queue handoff) is extracted into unit-testable functions; cpal::Error and SupportedStreamConfig are publicly constructible so the error paths are exercised without a device. This is not a design defect: the only untestable residue is the OS-level device probe itself, whose absence path is covered by the #[ignore] no-device integration test. Alternative verification: the #[ignore] no-device integration test on a host without an audio backend.
acceptanceCriteria: - 【Happy path】With `--features cpal-input`, open_default_microphone_source(format) opens the platform default input device and returns Ok(Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>) whose next_chunk fills an i16 buffer with captured PCM (>= 1 sample on a real device, verified by the #[ignore] integration test). The returned source is AsyncAudioSource + Send and can be stored as Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send> in AudioMixer (compile-time check). The O-001 unit tests pass: the 4 map_*_error helpers return NativeError with their prefixes for constructible cpal::Error values, and select_sample_format_handler accepts {I16,F32,U16} and rejects the other 12 SampleFormat variants with AudioFormatUnsupported.

- 【Error case】When no default input device exists, open_default_microphone_source returns Err(SipError) with a clear message (SipErrorKind::NativeError) instead of panicking (C051-Post typed-Err). When the requested AudioFormat cannot be matched by the device (non-convertible sample format), the function returns Err(SipError) describing the format mismatch (SipErrorKind::AudioFormatUnsupported) — asserted by the select_sample_format_handler unit tests, so a regression to panic!() or a wrong SipErrorKind fails CI.

- 【Edge case】With the feature disabled (default), the function and CpalMicrophoneSource are compiled out and the crate builds without cpal — no device capture is attempted and `cargo tree -e normal` shows no cpal (feature-additive invariant). Sample conversion clamps at i16 boundaries; an empty queue / zero-length buffer returns 0 without panicking. A 65536-sample buffer (AudioMixer boundary) drains without overflow.

### Goal
Resolve O-001 and finalize the real cpal device-backed microphone source: keep `open_default_microphone_source` (src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:173-179) returning `Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError>` backed by the platform default microphone behind the `cpal-input` feature, and close the ABC gap by unit-testing every error path (map_default_config_error / map_supported_configs_error / map_build_stream_error / map_play_error) and the unsupported-sample-format arm of build_input_stream, with the feature-gated integration test retained.

### Purpose
The `cpal-input` feature has been wired since P8-7 (Cargo.toml: `cpal-input = ["dep:cpal"]`), and the microphone source is the only RFC-required audio source that is device-backed. Downstream consumers (AudioMixer via P5-2, the audio_tap example via P8-6, AI TTS source insertion) rely on opening the default microphone as an AsyncAudioSource. The ABC inspection confirmed the happy-path machinery is complete but the error-contract (never-panic / typed-Err) is not enforced by any test — O-001 must be closed so the contract is provable.

### Motivation
P8-4 delivered the AsyncAudioSource adapter machinery under a no-new-dependencies constraint; P8-7 landed the cpal dependency and real capture, resolving the `[::STUB::] P8-7` marker. What remains is the ABC-mandated O-001 closure: cpal 0.18.1 exposes publicly constructible `cpal::Error` and `SupportedStreamConfig`, so the error paths are unit-testable without a device — the omission is a test-coverage defect, not an architectural limit. - cpal must be an optional dependency reachable only via `cpal-input`; default builds must not pull the cpal crate (feature-additive invariant). Cargo.toml:40 already declares `check-cfg = ['cfg(feature, values("cpal-input"))']`.

- No panics on device failure — all errors map to SipError (NativeError for device/stream, AudioFormatUnsupported for non-convertible sample formats). The O-001 unit tests must make a regression detectable.
- CI without audio hardware must not run the device integration test by default (#[ignore] + SI_PRS_TEST_AUDIO=1 gate).

### Goal
Resolve the five `[::STUB::] P9-1` markers by turning the example binaries (account_register, audio_tap, client_init, make_call, tts_source) from documentation stubs into runnable reference clients that parse CLI args and drive the real SipClient public API per RFC §41, backed by Layer 5 integration tests.

### Purpose
The examples are the crate's Layer 5 API documentation surface (N0052/N0065) — end users and the zasso ecosystem need runnable reference binaries showing how to initialize a client, register an account, place a call, tap audio, and inject a TTS source. Without them, the public API has no executable usage demonstration and the ABC inspection gaps (documented-but-unrunnable flows) cannot close.

### Motivation
Source ticket P1-3 deferred the example bodies because the CLI/PJSIP runtime was not yet available. That deferral produced INSPECTION_FLAGGED stubs. The required public types (SipClient, ClientConfig, AccountConfig, SipAccountHandle, OutgoingCallRequest, AsyncAudioSource) and the runtime command path (RuntimeHandle) now exist, so the examples can be made real. This is the final re-implementation round demanded by the inspection flag.

### Constraints
Examples consume the public API only (no internal-module reach-around beyond the documented RuntimeHandle command path). The `spec-examples` required-features gate stays for audio_tap until P9-2 provides subscribe_audio/AudioTapHandle. No new runtime dependencies for the examples (shared CLI parser uses std::env::args; clap stays behind the `cli` feature for the server binary). All five example main functions return Result and never panic (C056). `make test` must stay green.

Resolve the ABC-inspection omission O-001 in the already-implemented example binaries: add a source-inspection test (examples_have_result_returning_main) that pins every example main's return type to `Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>` (contract C056-Post), and update the C056-Post contract wording to match the actual pinned type. The examples are the crate's Layer 5 API documentation surface (N0052/N0065), so their error-propagation contract must be empirically pinned to make the documented-but-unrunnable gap undetectable no more.

### Motivation
The prior P9-1 round deferred `SipClient::add_account` and `subscribe_audio` because their dependency tickets (P10-3, P9-2) had not landed. Both have now landed (src/client.rs:219 `pub async fn add_account`, src/client.rs:349 `pub async fn subscribe_audio`), so the RuntimeHandle::submit_add_account workaround and the stale "a facade SipClient::add_account lands in P10-3" comment in examples/common/client.rs are now tech debt. evaluations.reason: Contract C056-Invariant requires src/runtime/reactor.rs to contain catch_unwind in its callback bridge so a panicking handler never unwinds across the boundary. The implementation does contain std::panic::catch_unwind (reactor.rs:133, 212, 238, 283, 318, 365, 395 wrapping command handlers), but NO test translates this invariant element: neither a source-inspection test greps reactor.rs for catch_unwind, nor does any test dispatch a panicking command to assert the reactor catches it and returns Err. The C056-Inv element is unpinned.

If every catch_unwind in src/runtime/reactor.rs were removed, no existing test would fail — the reactor command tests exercise happy-path and Err paths that never panic, and the example source-inspection tests (verify_spec_p9_1.rs:279) only scan examples/ files. A panicking command handler would then unwind out of the reactor command loop undetected, violating the C056-Invariant never-unwind-across-boundary requirement. Add the source-inspection and/or behavioral test to make the removal detectable.
